- A Sr. HELENS ANCTIONBER SID/IRONED FOR Asflamr. —On Friday, at the St. Helens Police Court, a summons • was heard, in which William Kirkham, auctioneer, valuer, and estate agent, was chayed with assaulting blacksmith named William Boardman.—Complainaat stated that on the evening of the 23rd ult. he went into a shop in Boundary-lane, for which defendant was agent. Mr. Kirk- ham was also there, and when he (complainant) left defen- dant followed him out,land, saying he had an old grudge against him, knocked him down and kicked h:ra savagely that one of his ribs were broken.—Defendant, who was re- presented by Mr. R. W. Thomas, denied the charge in NM. He proceeded to call witnesses, but after hear'ng the evi- dence of two persons the magistrates said they did not re- quire anything farther, and dismissed the summons. ALLEGED USE OF THE KNIFE AT ST. HELENS.—On Mon- day, at the St. Helens Police Court, an elderly ram named Michael Bennett, was charred with unlawfully wounding John Reck.—SuperintendeniJohnston said that cu Saturday night prosecutor and prisoner were together in a house in Westfield-street, kept by a couple named Ryan. Prisoner had lodged there for some time prior to a week age. The men sent out for a quart of beer, but as prisoner com- menced to use bad language she told him he had better go out, and opened the door for him to do so. Instead of going out, however, prisoner struck Mrs. Ryan, knocked her down, and kicked her. Prosecutor then interfered, and said to prisoner, "Strike me instead." At that time prisoner had a knife in his hand, and with it he a:ruck prosecutor a blow on the lower part of his body, cur t:ng his trousers, and in flicting a wound which had to oe stitched by a medical gentlemas.—Mrs. Joanna Ryan deposed to the above state. mem, after w.dch Dr. M•Nicoll said the wound was not a dangerous one. He thought prosecutor would ha able tO come down towards Thursday or Friday.—On the applica- tion of Supe,intendent Johnston, prisoner was remanded in custody until Thursday, when the prisoner alas again brought before the elan, and committed to the s-ssions for trial. He said in defence that he had been drank,snd knelt nothing of what had taken place. A FOOLISH RAILWAY CLERK: DISCHARGED AFTER 15 YEARS' SERVICE. —At St. Helens, on Prida•r, John Galdart. of Parr, who for the last 15 years has been em- ployed by .the Liorion and North-Western Railway Co., latter!,' in the mineral department at St. Helens, was sum- mon-o for travelling from Edge-hill, to St. Helens on the evening of the 11th nit., without having a ticket. —Mr. Preatoa, junr., from the solicitors' department, Lime-street, said the (intendant was seen to leave Edge-till Station by the 11-15 train, and he was followed by a detective. When he alighted at St. Helens he went into the general waiting- room for a few minutes, and then when ail the passengers had left tbe platform, he passed the ticket collector saying " Good night." Whoa he had get a hundred yards away the detective followed him and asked him for his ticket, to which he replied that he had not got one, and had no money to pay for one. Defendant had held a contract ticket to traal between St. Helens and Wigan, but not be- tween Liverpool and St. Helens. His last contract bad ex- pired about three months. He had received no.ice to leave the compatsy's service. Defendant did not app-ar. Mr. Preston asked the magistrates to deal severely with defen- dadt, as this manner of defrauding the company wt. 3 on the increase in this district.—The magistrates said they saw no reason why they should mitigate the pena:ty, a I defen- dant would be fined 40s. and 6s. costs.

GENTLEMEN,-1 thank you for the ready response to my application for the above appointment, and for the support which you so kindly premised me, for with the promises which 1 have received I should have had little doubt of success If a poll were to be demanded; but being a reasonable busi- ness man. I could not expect my supporters to waste their time to travel from the place where most of you reside to such an out of-the-way place in the division as Ormskirk. Wednesday is the day appointed for polling—lf a poll is demanded—and it takes place at Ormskirk. between the hours of Sam, and 4 p.m. When I asked you, gentlemen, for your support, I was under the impression that the election would be conducted within the lines of 7 and 8 Victoria, eh. 82, section 10 of which Act states that the nomination of candidates shall take plate at the most convenient place to the electors. I leave it to you, gentlemen, to judge whether Ormskirk is the most convenient place; may I ask you. I. it not the most inconvenient place within the West Derby Hundred? Then sectona 11 states that application can be made to Quarter Sesaions, giving an opportunity for candidates to ask the magistratea there assembled to appoint convenient places within the district, in case of a poll being taken. No doubt you are aware that Mr. Nash, at the instance of a Wigan candidate, made such an application at the Salford Hundred Sessions, for such an appointment of convenieat places, and pointed out that any candidate living in Ormskirk might block the booth with his supporters, as it is a well-known fact that It would be impossible to poll many more than 500 votes in the eight hours on Wednesday next ; and Mr. Nash also pointed out that as the Quarter Sessions at Liverpool com- menced on Tuesday. the Fifteenth instant. it would be too late to apply there, as the nomination was fixed for the Fourteenth; but such application was refuted. The whole arrangements of the poll are most unfair to four of the candidate. Under these circumstances, and being in the unfortunate position of a candidate situate furthest away from Ormsktrk. I hope I shall not lose any of the regard which I feel you have for me when I now inform you that I feel It my duty to withdraw from the contest. It is, indeed, a remarkable instance that the nomination should be fixed for Monday, the Fourteenth instant, and there is a Quarter Sessions at Liverpool on the Fifteenth, at which time an application might have been made to name convenient places for you to pall. Again thanking you for your generous support, I am, Gentlemen, your obedient servant, PERCY DAVIES. 1, Market-place, Warrington, Tenth January, 1884. B°R° WARRINGTON.—The England and Wales Markets and Fairs Temporary Order, 1883.— NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that a License has been granted to Mr. John Mainwaring to hold the following Pubic Sales of Fat Animals. On the 14th January, at the Eagle and Child Inn, Bridge- Street. On the 21st January, at the Norton Arms Hotel. Latchford. On the 28th January, at the Eagle and Child Inn, ,Bridge- street. Subject to the following conditions;— (1.) Animals exposed at such public sales so licensed, shall, after their arrival thereat, and before they are m toed therefrom, be marked by and at the expense of the owner, consignee, or other person exposing them; as fol- lows; Cattle.—By the clipping of a broad arrow, about five Inches long, on the left hind quarter of each of the cattle. SHEEP AND SWINE.—By the painting or stamping of the letter M, about six inches long, on the left side of each of the sheep or swine with the following composition, namely :—Rosin, five parts; oil of turpentine, two parts; and blue or red ochre, one part; melted and used warm ; or with some other adhesive composition of a blue or red colour. (ii.) Every animal that is exposed at the public sales so licensed, whether it is sold thereat or not, shall be slaugh- tered within six days after the day on which the sale is held. (iii.) Animals exposed at the public sales so licensed shall noll afterwards be exposed at any other public sale. Dated this 11112 January, 1884. WM. HY. BROOK, Town Clerk.
